Match or exceed the primary's class, reduce write volume, add indexes, or use Aurora (shared storage, minimal lag)
Application fails after a Multi-AZ failover
DNS caching - the endpoint stayed the same but the client cached the old IP
Client DNS TTL; Java networkaddress.cache.ttl; RDS event 'failover completed'
Set a short DNS TTL, reconnect on error, or front the DB with RDS Proxy which shortens failover impact
Application fails after a PITR or snapshot restore
Restore created a NEW instance with a NEW endpoint
The new instance endpoint; security group and parameter group of the restored instance
Repoint the app or move the CNAME; reattach the correct SG, parameter group, and option group
Parameter change had no effect
The parameter is static and needs a reboot, or the default parameter group is still attached
Parameter group apply type (static/dynamic) and pending-reboot status
Create a custom parameter group, associate it, and reboot the instance
High CPU with no obvious cause
Bad query plans, missing indexes, or a runaway session
Performance Insights DB load by wait/top SQL; CPUUtilization
Tune the top SQL, add indexes, or scale up; add read replicas for read-heavy load
OS-level memory or per-process detail needed
CloudWatch RDS metrics are host-aggregated only
Whether Enhanced Monitoring is enabled and at what granularity
Enable Enhanced Monitoring (1-60 s, agent-based, delivered to CloudWatch Logs)
Cannot connect from an application subnet
Security group, publicly accessible setting, or subnet group without a route
DB security group inbound on 3306/5432 from the app SG; DB subnet group AZs
Allow the app SG on the DB port; keep the DB private and reach it from inside the VPC or via a VPN/bastion-free Session Manager port forward
Cannot encrypt an existing database
Encryption can only be set at creation
Instance StorageEncrypted attribute
Snapshot -> copy snapshot with a KMS key -> restore from the encrypted copy -> cut over
Backups missing or PITR unavailable
Backup retention set to 0, or the instance is a read replica
Automated backup retention period (0-35 d)
Set retention to 1-35 days; note that changing from 0 causes a brief outage on some engines
Burst performance collapses on gp2 storage
Burst credits exhausted
BurstBalance metric
Move to gp3 or io2, or increase volume size for a higher baseline
decision_tables.rule_of_thumb: Connections -> RDS Proxy. Storage -> autoscaling. Lag -> replica size or Aurora. Restore -> new endpoint. Parameter -> reboot if static.

decision_tables.title: Which observability tool answers which question
rows: CloudWatch metrics + alarms
Is a resource healthy, saturated, or breaching a threshold right now?
threshold, notify, scale, utilization
Memory and disk need the agent; basic monitoring is 5-minute
CloudWatch Logs + metric filters
Did a specific message or error appear in application/system logs, and how often?
log message, error count, alarm on log
Metric filters do not backfill existing log data
CloudWatch Logs Insights
Ad hoc analysis across log groups - top errors, slowest requests, counts by field
query the logs, analyse, top N
Results retained 7 days; limited number of log groups per query
CloudWatch Synthetics
Is the endpoint available and correct from the outside, before users complain?
canary, proactive, user journey, broken link
Runs from AWS, costs per run; use for private endpoints inside a VPC too
Container Insights
How are my ECS/EKS clusters, nodes, pods, and tasks performing?
container, pod, cluster CPU/memory
EKS needs the CloudWatch Observability add-on
Managed Service for Prometheus + Managed Grafana
Open-source-native metrics and dashboards for Kubernetes at scale
Prometheus, PromQL, Grafana, remote write
Use when the stem explicitly says Prometheus or existing Grafana dashboards
X-Ray / Application Signals
Which microservice or downstream call is causing the latency or fault?
trace, distributed, service map, latency breakdown, SLO
Needs SDK/agent instrumentation or ADOT
CloudTrail
Who called which API, from where, when, and was it denied?
who deleted, audit, access denied, API call, compliance
Data events (S3 object, Lambda invoke) are off by default
AWS Config
What was this resource's configuration at a point in time, and is it compliant?
changed, configuration history, compliant, drift from policy
Config records configuration, not API calls or performance
Health Dashboard
Is AWS itself having an event that affects my resources?
AWS outage, scheduled maintenance, retirement notice
Account-level events also arrive via EventBridge
decision_tables.rule_of_thumb: Metrics = how is it. Logs = what did it say. Traces = where did the time go. CloudTrail = who did it. Config = what does it look like and is that allowed.

decision_tables.title: Systems Manager capability picker
rows: Run Command
Execute a command or script once across many nodes, targeted by tag or resource group
run a script on all instances, ad hoc, one-off
Managed nodes only; rate control defaults are MaxConcurrency 50 and MaxErrors 0 (one failure halts the run)
Automation
Multi-step runbook combining AWS API calls and instance actions, with branching and approvals
runbook, remediate, automated workflow, AMI patching pipeline
Needs an automation assume role; the default target for Config remediation and EventBridge
State Manager
Continuously enforce a desired state on a schedule
ensure, enforce, keep configured, drift back
Association with a schedule expression; can apply Ansible/DSC/agent updates
Patch Manager
Scan and install OS/application patches against a baseline
patch compliance, security updates, baseline
Patch group tag key is literally 'Patch Group'; runs inside a maintenance window
Maintenance Windows
Define an approved schedule and duration for disruptive tasks
approved change window, off-hours
Needs registered targets and registered tasks plus a service role
Inventory
Collect installed software, OS, network, and custom metadata from nodes
software inventory, what is installed, license audit
Uses a State Manager association; query with Athena/Resource Data Sync
Parameter Store
Hierarchical configuration and secret storage
config value, connection string, license key, SecureString
Standard tier free (4 KB value, 10,000 parameters); Advanced tier paid (8 KB value, 100,000 parameters, policies); no automatic rotation
Session Manager
Browser or CLI shell to instances without SSH, bastions, or open ports
no inbound ports, no bastion, audited shell access
No inbound SG rule required; log sessions to S3/CloudWatch; supports port forwarding
OpsCenter
Central queue of operational items (OpsItems) with runbooks attached
operational issues in one place, ticket-like
OpsItems can be created by CloudWatch alarms and EventBridge
Fleet Manager
Console-based OS management: file system, registry, users, performance counters
browse files, manage users, remote GUI-less admin
Managed node prerequisites still apply
Change Manager / Change Calendar
Approval workflow and blackout windows for operational changes
approval required, freeze window
Calendar states OPEN/CLOSED gate Automation execution
Quick Setup
One-click baseline SSM configuration across accounts and Regions
standardize across the organization
Uses Organizations; deploys roles, agent updates, inventory, patching
decision_tables.rule_of_thumb: Once = Run Command. Always = State Manager. Workflow = Automation. Shell = Session Manager. Config = Parameter Store.

decision_tables.title: CloudFormation protection, control, and inspection features
rows: DeletionPolicy
Retain, Snapshot, or Delete a resource when the STACK is deleted
Stack delete (and resource removal from the template)
Do not lose the database when the stack is deleted
UpdateReplacePolicy
Retain or Snapshot the OLD resource when an update replaces it
Stack update that requires replacement
Data must survive a property change that forces replacement
Stack policy
JSON that denies Update:Replace or Update:Delete on specific logical IDs during updates
Stack UPDATE only - never stack delete
Prevent accidental replacement of production resources during updates
Termination protection
Blocks the DeleteStack call entirely
Stack delete
Nobody should be able to delete this stack
CreationPolicy + cfn-signal
Waits for N success signals from instances before marking the resource created
Create (and rolling updates with an ASG)
Stack reports CREATE_COMPLETE before the application is actually ready
UpdatePolicy (AutoScalingRollingUpdate)
Controls batch size, pause time, and minimum healthy instances during an ASG update
Stack update touching an ASG
Update instances in batches without downtime
UpdatePolicy (AutoScalingReplacingUpdate)
Creates a whole new ASG and switches, rolling back the old one on failure
Stack update touching an ASG
Blue-green style replacement inside CloudFormation
Change set
Preview additions, modifications, deletions and whether replacement is required
Before executing an update
Show me what will change before I break production
Drift detection
Compares live resource configuration with the template
Any time, on demand or scheduled
Someone changed it in the console - detect only, does not remediate
Rollback triggers
Monitor CloudWatch alarms during the update and roll back automatically if they fire
During create/update
Automatically roll back if error rates spike after deployment
Service role
CloudFormation uses this role's permissions instead of the caller's
Every stack operation with a role set
Operators deploy without holding underlying resource permissions
Resource import
Bring existing resources under stack management without recreating them
Import operation
Manage manually created resources as IaC
decision_tables.rule_of_thumb: DeletionPolicy protects on delete, UpdateReplacePolicy protects on replace, stack policy protects during updates, termination protection protects the stack itself.

decision_tables.title: Auto Scaling policy picker and termination order
rows: Target tracking
Maintains a metric at a target value, creating and managing the alarms for you
Simplest continuous scaling on CPU, ALBRequestCountPerTarget, or network
Default answer for least operational overhead; uses instance warm-up, not cooldown
Step scaling
Different capacity adjustments for different breach magnitudes
Big spikes need bigger jumps than small ones
Uses warm-up; multiple step adjustments per alarm
Simple scaling
One adjustment then wait for the cooldown to expire
Legacy; only when the stem describes a single fixed adjustment with a cooldown
Cooldown default 300 s
Scheduled scaling
Change min/max/desired at specified times
Known business hours, batch windows, marketing events
Recurrence uses cron in UTC by default; supports time zones
Predictive scaling
Forecasts load from history and provisions ahead of it
Recurring daily/weekly cycles with long instance boot times
Needs at least 24 hours of data; forecast-only mode available for validation
Instance warm-up
Time before a new instance's metrics count toward the aggregate
Instances that need time to become representative
Replaces cooldown for target tracking and step policies
Health check grace period
Time before health checks can mark a new instance unhealthy
Long bootstrap
300 s in the console, 0 by default through the API/CLI/CloudFormation
Termination policy - default order
AZ imbalance first, then oldest launch template/configuration, then closest to the next billing hour, then random
Understanding which instance dies on scale-in
Override with OldestInstance, NewestInstance, ClosestToNextInstanceHour, AllocationStrategy, or a custom Lambda
Instance scale-in protection
Excludes specific instances from scale-in termination
Stateful or long-running jobs on specific instances
Set per instance or as a group default; does not protect from manual termination
Lifecycle hook
Pauses launch or termination for custom work
Register with a config system, drain connections, copy logs off
Heartbeat default 3,600 s, max 172,800 s (48 h); must call CompleteLifecycleAction
decision_tables.rule_of_thumb: Unless the question describes steps or a schedule, target tracking is the answer. Scale-in kills the oldest launch template in the biggest AZ.

decision_tables.title: Backup and restore mechanism picker
trigger_words: restore to a point in time
rows: AWS Backup
EC2, EBS, RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, EFS, FSx, S3, Storage Gateway, VMware, SAP HANA, Redshift
Backup plan rules with cron, lifecycle to cold storage (min 90 days there), retention per rule; cross-Region and cross-account copy
Restores to a new resource; supports restore testing plans and Backup Audit Manager reports
AWS Backup Vault Lock
Any vault

Governance mode (removable at any time by a principal with the delete-lock permission, no cooling-off) or Compliance mode (cooling-off of at least 3 days set at creation, immutable to everyone including root afterwards)
Only compliance mode prevents early deletion and retention shortening - it is the WORM answer; governance mode is only a guardrail
Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (DLM)
EBS snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs
Policy by tag with an interval schedule, retention count or age, cross-Region copy, fast snapshot restore
Standard snapshot restore into a new volume
Manual EBS snapshot
One volume
Kept until deleted
Incremental storage, full restore; lazy-loaded unless FSR is enabled
RDS automated backups
One DB instance
0-35 days, daily backup window plus 5-minute transaction logs
Enables PITR; deleted with the instance unless you retain automated backups
RDS manual snapshot
One DB instance/cluster
Kept until deleted, survives instance deletion, copyable cross-Region and cross-account
Restores to a NEW instance with a NEW endpoint
RDS / DynamoDB PITR
One database or table
Continuous, 35-day window (DynamoDB); RDS window equals the retention period
Restores to a NEW instance/table - the application must be repointed
S3 versioning
Bucket
Every overwrite/delete keeps the prior version; lifecycle rules expire noncurrent versions
Recover by deleting the delete marker or copying an old version forward; MFA Delete hardens it
S3 Object Lock
Bucket (requires versioning)
Retention period or legal hold, governance or compliance mode
Objects cannot be overwritten or deleted for the retention period - regulatory WORM
S3 replication (CRR/SRR)
Bucket to bucket, same or cross Region/account
Continuous, near real time; requires versioning on both and an IAM role
Not retroactive - use S3 Batch Replication for existing objects; RTC gives a 15-minute SLA
EBS Fast Snapshot Restore
Snapshot per AZ
Enabled per snapshot per AZ, charged per AZ-hour
Removes the lazy-load first-touch latency for fast RTO
Aurora Backtrack / cloning
Aurora MySQL / Aurora clusters
Backtrack window in hours (MySQL); clones are copy-on-write
Backtrack rewinds the SAME cluster in place - no restore needed; clones are fast test copies
decision_tables.rule_of_thumb: Central policy across services = AWS Backup. Immutability = Vault Lock or Object Lock compliance mode. EBS-only automation = DLM. Any restore creates something new except Aurora Backtrack.

decision_tables.title: Route 53 records, routing, health checks, and Resolver
rows: Alias record
AWS-internal pointer to an ELB, CloudFront, S3 website, API Gateway, Global Accelerator, or another record in the zone
You need a record at the zone apex (example.com) or free queries
CNAME cannot exist at the apex; alias supports Evaluate Target Health
CNAME record
Maps a name to another DNS name
Subdomains pointing at external hostnames
Not allowed at the apex; charged per query; cannot coexist with other record types for the same name
Weighted routing
Splits traffic by assigned weights
Blue-green, canary, A/B testing
Weight 0 removes a record from rotation; all-zero weights makes all records eligible
Latency routing
Sends users to the Region with the lowest measured latency
Multi-Region active-active performance
Latency, not geography - not a compliance control
Failover routing
Primary with a health check, secondary takes over when unhealthy
Active-passive DR
The primary record MUST have a health check attached or failover never happens
Geolocation routing
Routes by the user's country/continent/state
Data residency, localization, licensing
Always configure a default record for unmatched locations
Geoproximity routing
Routes by distance with an adjustable bias
Shift load between Regions gradually by geography
Requires Route 53 traffic flow
Multivalue answer
Returns up to 8 healthy records at random
Simple client-side load spreading with health checks
Not a substitute for a load balancer
Endpoint health check
Route 53 public checkers probe an IP or domain over HTTP/HTTPS/TCP
Public endpoints
Checkers are on the public internet - the endpoint must be publicly reachable; failure threshold default 3, interval 30 s (or 10 s fast)
Calculated health check
Parent check over child checks with a threshold
Consider the service healthy if X of Y components are up
Up to 255 child health checks; the children can themselves be CloudWatch alarm checks for private endpoints
CloudWatch alarm health check
Health derived from an alarm state
Private resources, custom metrics, or anything the public checkers cannot reach
The correct answer whenever the endpoint is private
Resolver inbound endpoint
On-premises DNS forwards INTO the VPC to resolve AWS names
On-prem systems must resolve private hosted zone or VPC endpoint names
Needs ENIs with IPs in your subnets and firewall rules allowing UDP/TCP 53
Resolver outbound endpoint + rules
VPC queries are forwarded OUT to on-premises resolvers
Applications in AWS must resolve corporate names
Forwarding rules can be shared across accounts with RAM
Private hosted zone
Names resolvable only inside associated VPCs
Internal service naming
Requires enableDnsSupport and enableDnsHostnames on the VPC
Resolver DNS Firewall
Blocks or alerts on DNS queries to specified domains
Prevent data exfiltration and known-bad domain resolution
Rule group order matters; managed domain lists available
Query logging
Records DNS queries for public zones (CloudWatch Logs, us-east-1) or Resolver queries per VPC
Audit and diagnose name resolution
VPC Flow Logs never show resolver DNS traffic
decision_tables.rule_of_thumb: Apex = alias. Private endpoint = CloudWatch alarm health check. On-prem resolves AWS = inbound endpoint. AWS resolves on-prem = outbound endpoint.

decision_tables.title: Security and compliance service picker
rows: GuardDuty
CloudTrail management events, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs by default; optionally S3 data events, EKS audit logs, EC2/EBS malware, RDS logins, Lambda network
Threat findings with severity (crypto mining, credential exfiltration, port scanning, anomalous API use)
Findings to EventBridge -> Lambda or SSM Automation to isolate, snapshot, or revoke
Inspector
EC2 (SSM agent or agentless), ECR images, Lambda functions and layers
CVE vulnerability findings with an Inspector score and remediation
Patch via Patch Manager, rebuild images with Image Builder; findings flow to Security Hub
Macie
S3 objects for PII and sensitive data
Sensitive data discovery findings and bucket-level public/encryption posture
Tag, restrict, or encrypt the buckets; findings to Security Hub and EventBridge
Security Hub
Findings from all the above plus Config, Access Analyzer, Firewall Manager, and partners
ASFF findings, standards compliance scores (FSBP, CIS, PCI, NIST), insights
Automation rules and EventBridge to custom actions; cross-Region aggregation
AWS Config
Resource configuration state and change history
Compliant / non-compliant per rule, configuration timeline
Auto-remediation with an SSM Automation document; conformance packs for standards
Trusted Advisor
Account-wide best-practice checks
